Base models are trained on 'large datasets of labeled art.' No explicit opt-out mechanism is documented for model training.

flags: A Nudge Security profile lists SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, HIPAA, PCI, and FedRAMP compliance plus CSA STAR Level 1, but none of these are documented on Gencraft's own website. No trust center page was found. These claims are unverified.

Vendor identity: gencraft.com (Seattle-based; AI product launched in 2023, designed by an ex-Hive.ai product designer). Some company databases (e.g. Tracxn) list a 2012 incorporation date, but the Gencraft AI art/video product itself is a 2023 launch and should not be characterized as a 14-year-old platform.

A Common Sense Media evaluation (Sept 2024) flagged that 'Personal information is sold or rented to third parties' and user data is 'leveraged to track and target advertisements on other third-party websites.' This is a significant privacy risk not clearly disclosed on the vendor's domain.
Whether user-generated custom model training images are subsequently used to improve foundation models is not explicitly documented.

Gencraft appears unfunded/bootstrapped and its AI product launched in 2023, making it an early-stage startup. Limited resources for formal certification programs are typical at this stage; the absence of certifications does not necessarily indicate a compliance failure.
Gencraft relies on Google Analytics/Firebase and other Google services for operations. Customer data is passed to third parties for analytics and advertising purposes.

Despite claims in the Nudge Security profile, no vendor-domain documentation exists for SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certification. Either the Nudge profile is inaccurate or the certifications are not publicly available.
